subject: alchemistWorkbench
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: alchemist's workbench with potions, books, scales and herbs.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I need to plan a full TypeScript module for this prop group — since there's no creature involved, I'll still add a single root joint called "base" at the origin just to satisfy the builder's requirement of at least one root joint, keeping the style aligned with a Mondstadt/Sumeru-inspired fantasy aesthetic.

I'm pulling in toon, glow, and clockwork kits for the cel-shaded ink look with brass accents. The design is an alchemist's workbench scene: a staged table with a balance scale, books, glowing potions and alembic flasks, mortar and pestle, hanging herbs, a shelf of bottles, a floating elemental Vision orb with gold frame, a windrose emblem on the front panel, and drawer details — all built on a stone/rug platform base.

Now I'm working out precise coordinates for the tabletop, octagonal base platform, and the back rack with its shelf and herb rail, targeting roughly 180+ parts total, then setting up builder helper functions to place joints and parts efficiently.

I'm thinking through paint density for the cel-shaded texture atlas — balancing texel resolution against sheet size, and deciding whether 2048px gives crisp enough results without making the atlas too heavy, probably settling on keeping it closer to the default 1024.

Now I'm sketching out the material palette: wood using a grain paint with shadow derived from the lit color, with the grain axis oriented differently for the tabletop versus the legs.

For trim and metal, I'm choosing flat gold tones instead of a lit metal shader to keep the Genshin-style aesthetic and avoid double-lighting. For the rug runner, I'm planning a flat plane geometry lying on the table with an SVG texture carrying a Genshin-inspired motif like a windrose pattern with teal and gold coloring.

I'm mapping out the remaining textures needed: an alchemy circle emblem for the table apron, glowing rune pages for an open book, a couple of potion label variants (leaf and flame themed), herb cards showing a leaf, flower, and tied bundle, and finally an elemental vision gem shape with a gold frame.

For that gem vision I'm planning to build it from a scaled octahedron geometry, flat-shaded and glowing, surrounded by a torus ring frame and small floating glowing particles. Then I still need a parchment scroll texture, a pinned blueprint/recipe note with diagrams, and a solution for glass bottles—since materials are opaque, I'll fake the glass by making the bottles solid-colored lathe shapes matching the liquid color with a subtle inner glow instead of true transparency.

For the bottles, I'll add a stylized highlight using a white streak decal texture applied to the curved surface, plus a cork and gold cap rim, keeping some bottles glowing and others flat cel-shaded for variety.

Setting up helper functions...

Now working through the lathe profile logic: points run outward from the axis and back, with the axis points at top and bottom closing the loop naturally since the shape always closes.

I'm being careful with smoothing since tight profiles near the axis risk corners crossing—better to avoid heavy smoothing and instead design enough manual points, keeping segments around 10-12 for a low-poly look and starting to sketch out actual bottle profile shapes.

Sketching a round flask profile point-by-point, with a separate cork cylinder and gold rim, then thinking through other bottle variants like a tall vial, hex flask, and conical Erlenmeyer. I'm planning a reusable bottle(profile, color, at, opts) helper along with a highlight decal texture using an SVG with a curved white stroke and dot on a transparent background.

For the highlight decal, I'm positioning it on the bottle's front-left upper surface, projected against a direction vector so it reads as a glass glare. For glowing potions, since the glass is opaque I'm considering making the whole bottle body glow with moderate strength combined with the highlight decal and a dark outline, or alternatively using a pale glass color near the neck/shoulder while the lower body carries the main potion color.

For the liquid-in-glass effect, I'm splitting the bottle into two lathes sharing the same profile: a glass lathe covering the full shape, and a liquid lathe clipped at the fill height with a slightly larger radius so it peeks through as the visible liquid with a flat meniscus top, while the glass shows pale above the fill line.

Now I'm moving on to the balance scale — planning a brass base cylinder, post, and beam, with pans suspended by thin chain-like rods from the beam ends.

Still working out the tilt geometry...

For the books stack, I'm planning a helper function that builds each book from a colored cover box, an inset cream page block, gold spine bands, and a title plate, with yaw rotation applied to position the child parts correctly.

Still designing book geometry...

Working out plane orientation...

So I'll use `dir:[sin t, cos t, 0], axis:"z", up:[0,0,-1]` to make the plane face upward with its drawing top pointing away from the viewer. I'm also reconsidering the glow approach -- I shouldn't glow the whole page texture since that would wash out the dark parts; instead I should keep the paper normal and apply glow only to a separate rune overlay layer.

For the hanging herb bundles, I'm figuring out how to construct them from a knot point on a rail with fanned-out stems and leaf cards, working through frame orientations and lean angles to get the stems hanging and splaying naturally.

Still working through the ring geometry...

I'm checking whether cards need flow settings — default flow with the facing axis should work fine with cross:true for visibility, plus some rng variety. Then I'm thinking about the leaf textures, like HERB1 and HERB2, and how the hanging bundle roots attach at the knot point.

Now I'm planning three sprig bundle types: a green leaf sprig, a purple lavender, and a third option, each drawn stem-first toward the knot. I'm also considering adding potted plants to the table, like a glowing Glaze Lily with extruding petals.

Writing petal outline coordinates...

Now I'm designing an Elemental Vision prop for the table: since extrude can't have holes, I'll build it as a gold diamond-shaped plate backing, a glowing teal gem (flattened octahedron) on top, and a gold torus ring around it, all mounted on a small stand.

I'm thinking I could let this Vision float above the book stack instead, with orbiting glowing rings and spiral wind-swirl sprites to sell an Anemo wind effect, using a sweep along a spiral path for the thin glowing trail. Then I'm moving on to another prop idea: an alembic/retort setup with a copper bulb body on a tripod over a brass burner with a flame.

Still refining the alembic: a curved neck sweeping down into a receiving flask, glowing orange teardrop flame, glass flasks with glowing green liquid inside connected by a bent copper-ish tube. After that I'm sketching a mortar and pestle — stone-grey lathed mortar with a slanted green pestle.

Then I'm adding a melted candle with a small glowing flame and wax drips on a gold holder, plus a few glowing crystal clusters on a rock in a dish to round out the scene without overcomplicating things. Finally I'm sizing the table slab, a wood-grain box roughly 1.7×0.07×0.78, positioning its top surface around y=0.9.

For the table structure, I'm setting leg heights at 0.84 with square box tops, adding front/side aprons, and giving the front apron two drawers with brass knobs, keyholes, and an emblem. Below that I'm placing a lower shelf around y=0.25 holding a crate of bottled herbs, a sack, and a small barrel for extra texture, and at the back I'm building a rack with posts rising from the tabletop to y=1.75, a carved gold crossbar on top, a mid-shelf at y=1.28 for jars and bottles, and a herb rail at y=1.62 with hanging herbs visible through the open back.

Now I'm thinking about adding a parchment board with pinned notes centered on the back panel between the posts, spanning roughly y=0.95 to 1.7 in dark wood, sitting behind the shelf. I'm considering keeping bottles toward the sides of the shelf (|x|>0.3) and reserving the center for a hung blueprint scroll, with the floating vision positioned in front of it near x=0, y=1.15 -- though that feels cluttered, so I'm reconsidering having the vision hover directly over the table's center instead.

I also want a hanging Mondstadt-style lantern -- gold frame, cylindrical glass glow -- suspended by a chain from the top crossbar, but I need to adjust its position so it doesn't collide with the bottle tops on the shelf below, possibly shifting it in x or z to clear the vision and shelf items.

Mirroring a lantern on the left post too, with brackets extending slightly forward from each post. I'm setting overall height with posts up to 1.85, a gold-finialed crossbar at 1.82 with a Windblume crest emblem, keeping proportions sensible relative to the 0.9-high table. For the base, I'm adding an octagonal stone platform, radius 1.25 and height 0.06, to anchor everything.

Expanding the platform scene with the table positioned at origin, plus a stool to the front-left for height variety, and a small barrel with iron bands and a glowing potion bottle to the right, checking each item's radius stays within the platform's bounds.

Checking positions again, I bump the platform radius up to 1.4 so the stool and barrel both clear with some margin, then work out the octagon's flat-to-flat radius. I'm building the platform's lathe profile with a tiered base and slight sink, plus a stone texture with patches and cracks for the surface material.

I want a thin glowing teal torus ring embedded in the platform, lying flat, plus a rune-circle decal plane on the floor for a transmutation-circle glow effect, mostly hidden under the table but visible around the edges. Now I'm adjusting vertical offsets slightly to avoid z-fighting between the platform surface and the glowing rune plane.

Let me set up the coordinate baseline: platform floor at F=0.09, table top at T=F+0.84=0.93, and build everything relative to those constants. I'm also planning out the SVG textures I'll need — rug cloth, gold crest emblem, page lines, cover ornament, and an open page texture with text.

Continuing to list out the remaining textures: rune glow overlay, transmutation circle floor glow, leaf and lavender sprigs, glass highlight streak, a parchment potion label with icon, and a blueprint note. That rounds out to roughly a dozen textures, so I'll keep atlas sizes moderate (128-512px) to manage memory, and some of these will double as emissive glow maps for lit parts. Now I'm writing the concentric-circle SVG for the transmutation circle texture.

Generating SVG markup...

Defining wood grain variants...

Defining helper functions for building geometry primitives—boxes, cylinders, and spheres—attached to bones with configurable position and scale options.

Adding more helpers now: a local-frame function that converts coordinates based on origin and yaw rotation, and starting a book-building function that uses this frame to position cover and trim geometry.

Adjusting pages box...

Working out the orientation math for the title plane's up vector, deriving it from the yaw rotation so the text reads correctly relative to the spine.

That rotation order would yaw about the wrong axis and tilt the normal instead, so I'll stick with the dir/up approach instead. For the cover details, I'll skip the spine label and just add corner caps and a gold clasp strap positioned at one side of the book.

Now I'm sketching out the plan for shelf contents: roughly 8 parts per book times 5 books gives about 40 parts, so I want a cheap reusable spine-book helper that builds a box plus gold bands and a label rect, and a separate bottle-building function with profile, fill, and liquid parameters. Writing profile clipping helper...

I'll just nudge the liquid base slightly rather than overthink the z-fighting. For the bottle, I need to make sure the lathe profile starts correctly with the base point, color the glass shell pale with a glowing liquid inside, and add extras like a cork — deriving the neck radius and top from the profile's last points to size a tapered cylinder for it.

For the neck I'll add a short wider ring to suggest a gold band, and for the highlight decal I'm placing it on whichever surface is actually visible — targeting the liquid part if it exists in front of the glass, since a decal buried under glass would be hidden, and orienting its direction and size relative to the bottle's radius and height.

Now I'm positioning the label decal on the front-right of the bottle near the top of the liquid, sized proportionally to the bottle's widest radius, and nudging its lift slightly higher than the highlight decal to avoid z-fighting where they overlap. I'm also tallying up the potion count — six on the table and six on the shelf.

With roughly a dozen bottles each needing glass, liquid, cork, ring, highlight, and label parts, I'm estimating around 70 total parts, which seems reasonable. I'm sketching out a few different bottle silhouette profiles — a rounded one with a narrow neck and lip, a taller slender one with a longer neck, and I'm starting on a cone-shaped erlenmeyer flask variant.

Still writing profile coordinates...
